title: Which Precedent Governs a Multi-Year Prepay Discount
scenario_text:
You are on Deal Desk at Saxby Logistics. AE Karim Fadel is structuring a new-logo deal for 'Trellis Freight': a 3-year term with full upfront prepayment, and he wants a 30% discount plus a 60-day payment terms extension. He cites two prior deals as precedent.

Active policy: Pricing & Terms Policy PT-6, effective 2024-07-01. For multi-year prepaid deals: discounts up to 20% are AE/Manager approved; 21-30% requires VP Sales; any non-standard payment terms (beyond net-30) require the Finance Controller regardless of discount. Discount and payment-terms approvals are independent and BOTH must be obtained when both apply.

Precedent A (deal-desk log): 2024-08-11, 'Marlowe Shipping,' 3-year prepaid, 28% discount, net-30 terms. Approved by VP Sales only. Note: "Standard net-30; no Controller needed. PT-6."

Precedent B (deal-desk log): 2024-09-02, 'Denby Cargo,' 3-year prepaid, 18% discount, net-60 terms. Approved by Manager (for discount) + Finance Controller (for terms). Note: "Sub-20% discount, but net-60 triggers Controller. PT-6."

Karim argues: "Marlowe got 28% signed off by VP Sales alone with no Controller — Trellis is basically the same profile, so VP Sales should be enough here too."

All three deals are under PT-6. Trellis has no special strategic-logo flag.
question: What approval path does the Trellis Freight deal require?
choices: VP Sales approval alone, following the Marlowe Shipping precedent, since both are ~30% multi-year prepaid deals.
VP Sales approval for the 30% discount AND Finance Controller approval for the net-60 terms, because both PT-6 triggers apply and each requires its own sign-off.
Manager approval for the discount plus Finance Controller for the terms, following the Denby Cargo precedent for a deal with extended payment terms.
Finance Controller approval alone, since the non-standard payment terms are the highest-authority requirement and subsume the discount approval.
